label: PR 6 with issue #22 folded in, a vitest 5 unblock, and four rounds correcting my own review tooling
decisions: Issue #22 folded into PR 6 as one branch rather than landing ahead of it: the deletion route is born gated instead of being retrofitted into a policy that did not exist when it was written
The project deletion path holds the artist's own token, never service_role, so no RLS-bypassing credential enters an app runtime -- ADR 0003

Storage-side byte-swap closed by policy rather than credential custody: the insert policy refuses a write to a key a source_images row already cites. Same remedy the row side already chose, where source_images has no DELETE policy for the same delete-then-insert reason -- ADR 0003

Deletion cannot be one transaction: Supabase's protect_objects_delete trigger refuses direct SQL deletion from storage.objects for every role, so a security definer function is impossible. Measured, and pinned by a test so a change upstream reopens the design -- ADR 0003

Objects before rows, and completeness judged by end state rather than removal count. Storage answers 200 [] for an already-absent key, so counting removals made a project permanently undeletable once an artist deleted their own object directly -- ADR 0003
API route handlers check auth only, not the acknowledgement. It is a demo disclaimer about what the UI shows, and keeping it out means issue #27 need not touch handlers

Refusal vocabulary is two codes: 401 for no usable artist session including a cross-app operator cookie, 404 for every ownership failure. 403 deliberately absent so no account can confirm another's project ids

The synthetic-data acknowledgement moves to the studio login page and off operations, so an artist landing directly on the studio needs no round trip to entry. Parked as issue #27; the ack-cookie-lifetime question is recorded there, unanswered

The vitest-axe matcher augmentation moves to a .d.ts so skipLibCheck covers it, matching the suppression @testing-library/jest-dom's incompatible declaration already receives. Unblocked the vitest 4 -> 5 major that dependabot had grouped with six patch bumps
Two worktrees, not three: the DB/app track kept together because #22 and PR 6 rewrite the same two files, with PR 11 isolated as the only genuinely parallel track

retro.went_well: Measuring beat reasoning three times, and each time the measurement killed a design I would otherwise have built. The protect_objects_delete trigger eliminated the security-definer approach outright; batch-deleting an absent key returning 200 [] is what made the deletion lockout visible; and proving pulls/<N>/comments and issues/<N>/comments are disjoint collections is what showed a verification step had the same blind spot as the bug it was written to close. Review earned its cost on #29 in particular: two P1s, both real defects in code written this session, both in failure paths that 92 passing tests never exercised. Laurie's push-back on 'vitest 5 cannot be adopted' was right and took one command to act on -- the suite already passed, and only tsc was failing.
retro.improve: The comment-posting bug is the one worth sitting with. `gh api -f body=@file` adds the string literally, so two dispositions on #29 posted as the eleven characters of a filename -- and I reported both as successfully posted, because the API answered 201 with an html_url. I verified that a write had happened, not what it wrote, and it took Laurie noticing an unresolved thread for the real state to surface. The same shape recurred twice more: I framed a design question on a false premise, calling the synthetic-data notice a consent record when packages/auth/src/ack.ts says in terms that it is a demo disclaimer, and I asserted vitest 5 could not be adopted without running the suite that disproved it. Three cases of concluding from inference where one command was available. The correction itself then needed four commits, including a fix whose own diff-based check would have reported MISMATCH on every correctly posted comment.
retro.tooling_suggestion: `pnpm --filter <pkg> test -u` silently swallows the flag: pnpm consumes it and prints its own CLI help, so a snapshot update reads as a broken command rather than a missing `--`. .claude/rules/workflow.md already says to pass extra args through the script for e2e; generalising that line to every script would have saved a cycle. Separately, markdownlint-cli2's glob does not honour .gitignore, so `pnpm lint:md` and therefore `pnpm check:all` are red locally for anyone with docs/temp-references/ present -- 44 errors in files git never sees, which erodes the pre-commit hook's value.

note: Cost, durations and the 87% context figure are from /usage. context_over_150k_pct and the skills breakdown are its last-24h figures across all local sessions, not this session alone -- the same panel attributes 60% of last-24h usage to subagent-heavy sessions and 2% to Explore, but this session spawned no subagents at all. parallel_agents is 1 accordingly: a worktree was prepared for PR 11 and rebased twice, but no session ever ran in it. Prompt cache held 99% of input tokens across 269 requests with no misses. Laurie also merged four dependabot PRs (#23, #24, #25, #26); #26 bundled a vitest 4 -> 5 major with six patch bumps, which is what PR #28 existed to unblock, and the underlying grouping in .github/dependabot.yml is still unrestricted so it will recur on the next major. Issue #27 filed and parked. Five review findings across three PRs: four fixed, one declined as both out of diff and factually wrong about vitest-axe's peer range. Two of the three PRs merged today were repairs of my own errors rather than planned work. The churn split into `refinement` and `avoidable_error` is reconstructed: this record was written when the two were one `claude_error` bucket (60%), and the split was derived afterwards from this record's own retro rather than from the session.
